svg.content: <mxfile host="app.diagrams.net" scale="1" border="0"> <diagram name="Social Media Feed Architecture" id="6TTMjznKKu_IRPnFUPJP"> <mxGraphModel dx="5103" dy="2890" grid="1" gridSize="10" guides="1" tooltips="1" connect="1" arrows="1" fold="1" page="1" pageScale="1" pageWidth="850" pageHeight="1100" math="0" shadow="0"> <root> <mxCell id="0" /> <mxCell id="1" parent="0" /> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-1" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=24;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="Social Media Feed — Data Model, Indexing &amp; Fan-out" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="36" width="1700" x="40" y="8" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-2" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Goal:</b> show every user a fast home feed of posts from people they follow &nbsp;|&nbsp; <b>Rule:</b> reads outnumber writes ~50:1, so do the heavy work when someone POSTS &nbsp;|&nbsp; <b>Example scale (assumed):</b> 100M daily users × 10 opens ≈ 11.5k feed reads/s (peak ~35k) · 20M posts/day ≈ 230/s · 200 avg followers → 4B feed inserts/day ≈ 46k/s" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="44" width="1880" x="40" y="48" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-3" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#b26a00;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#b26a00;" value="START HERE — the one question this design answers" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="140" width="1910" x="20" y="100" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-4" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#f8cecc;strokeColor=#b85450;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Problem:</b> a home feed = newest posts from the ~500 people I follow. Building it on EVERY open means a lookup across 500 authors plus a sort — too slow for 1B opens a day." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="85" width="590" x="40" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-5" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Decision:</b> do the work when someone POSTS (write path), so opening the app (read path) is one fast lookup." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="85" width="590" x="680" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-6" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>But:</b> a celebrity post would need 50M feed inserts. So the plan is a HYBRID: push for normal users, pull for celebrities." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="85" width="590" x="1320" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-7" edge="1" parent="1" source="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-4" target="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-6" value="but"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-9" parent="1" style="rounded=0;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=none;dashed=1;dashPattern=8 4;strokeColor=#1a56a0;verticalAlign=top;align=left;spacingLeft=12;spacingTop=4;fontStyle=1;fontSize=14;fontColor=#1a56a0;" value="A · DATA — which store for which data, and how each is indexed" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="500" width="1910" x="20" y="260" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-10" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=11;fontColor=#222222;spacing=4;" value="<b>Blue</b> = the table and its columns &nbsp;·&nbsp; <b>Green</b> = how it is indexed &nbsp;·&nbsp; <b>Yellow</b> = why this store, and what it costs" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="24" width="1800" x="40" y="290" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-11" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>1 · USERS — SQL</b><br>users(<br>user_id PK, handle UNIQUE, email UNIQUE,<br>display_name, created_at,<br>follower_count, is_celebrity)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="40" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-12" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>B-tree on user_id</b> + <b>UNIQUE B-tree on handle and email.</b> Answers "find user at login" in one lookup, and no two people can own one handle." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="40" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-13" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Why SQL:</b> small data that needs strong consistency. <i>Cost:</i> hard to shard — fine, users are our smallest table." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="40" y="625" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-14" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>2 · FOLLOWS — SQL or wide-column</b><br>follows(follower_id, followee_id, created_at)<br>copy A: PK (follower_id, followee_id)<br>copy B: PK (followee_id, follower_id)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="355" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-15" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Two composite indexes, one per direction.</b> A answers "who do I follow?", B answers "who follows me?" (fan-out needs it). One index cannot serve both." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="355" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-16" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Why not a graph DB?</b> We only need 1-hop lists. <i>Cost:</i> every follow = 2 writes. Add a graph DB later only for "people you may know"." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="355" y="625" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-17" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>3 · POSTS — wide-column / sharded SQL</b><br>posts(post_id PK, author_id, text,<br>media_ids, created_at, like_count…)<br>post_id = time-sortable ID (Snowflake-style)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="670" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-18" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>PK post_id</b> → get one post. <b>(author_id, post_id DESC)</b> → a profile page, already sorted. Time-sortable IDs mean NO extra created_at index." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="670" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-19" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Why NoSQL:</b> huge, append-heavy, read by key. <i>Cost:</i> no ad-hoc joins — every new question needs its own table or index." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="670" y="625" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-20" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>4 · FEED — Redis sorted set</b><br>key = feed:{user_id}<br>member = post_id<br>score = post time (or rank score)<br>keep only the newest ~800 ids" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="985" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-21" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Sorted set (skip list):</b> ZREVRANGE returns a page in O(log N + page). IDs only — tiny; bodies come from a post cache." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="985" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-22" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Why Redis:</b> sub-millisecond reads. <i>Cost:</i> RAM is expensive; the feed is a rebuildable cache, not the source of truth." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="985" y="625" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-23" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>5 · MEDIA — object storage + CDN</b><br>blob: media/{id}/original · 1080 · thumb<br>DB keeps only media_id, URL, type, size" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="1300" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-24" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>No index inside storage</b> — fetched by key (URL). A CDN caches popular files near users. Resize / transcode runs async." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="1300" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-25" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Why not in the DB:</b> big blobs would bloat it. <i>Cost:</i> new sizes appear a little later; storage + CDN bandwidth bill." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="1300" y="625" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-26" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=11;fillColor=#dae8fc;strokeColor=#6c8ebf;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>6 · SEARCH — Elasticsearch / OpenSearch</b><br>doc: post_id, text, hashtags, author, time<br>doc: user_id, handle, display_name" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="150" width="275" x="1615" y="325" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-27" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#d5e8d4;strokeColor=#82b366;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Inverted index</b> (word → posts) for text; <b>edge n-gram index</b> for typing "ank…" in people search. Fed async from Kafka." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="275" x="1615" y="490" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-28" parent="1" value="<b>Why separate:</b> SQL LIKE "%word%" scans everything. <i>Cost:</i> eventually consistent (searchable after seconds) + one more system to keep in sync." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" value="<b>Push or pull?</b> HYBRID. Push (fan-out on write) for normal authors, pull (fan-out on read) for celebrities. <i>Why:</i> push makes reads instant; pull avoids 50M writes per post. <i>Cost:</i> two code paths and a merge step." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="185" width="275" x="40" y="1830" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-94" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Fan-out on write vs on read?</b> On write, cost = followers per POST (4B inserts/day — fine). On read, cost = followees per OPEN (1B opens × 500 lookups — too much). <i>So:</i> pay at write while the multiplier is small." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="185" width="275" x="355" y="1830" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-95" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Celebrity with 50M followers?</b> One post = 50M inserts — at 46k/s that is ~18 minutes of the whole fleet, mostly into inactive feeds. Skip push above the threshold; readers pull. <i>Extra saving:</i> push only to followers active in the last ~7 days." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="185" width="275" x="670" y="1830" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-96" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>How is the home feed generated?</b> Precomputed ID list in Redis (⑤a) + pulled celebrity posts (⑧), merged (⑨), hydrated (⑩). <i>Why IDs only:</i> the list is tiny, and edits or deletes show instantly because bodies are read fresh." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="185" width="275" x="985" y="1830" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-97" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Chronological or recommended?</b> Start chronological: simple, explainable, cheap (sort by post_id). Recommended: better engagement, but costly ML, hard to debug, filter-bubble risk. <i>Offer both:</i> "Following" and "For you"." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="185" width="275" x="1300" y="1830" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-98" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#fff2cc;strokeColor=#d6b656;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>How do we rank?</b> Two stages: (1) a cheap candidate pool (~500 from feed + celebrities), (2) score = recency × closeness to author × engagement × post type, then diversify so one author cannot dominate. <i>Budget:</i> ~50–100 ms." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="185" width="275" x="1615" y="1830" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-99" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=13;fontColor=#222222;spacing=4;" value="<b>EDGE CASES — what a good architect asks next</b>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="24" width="900" x="40" y="2030" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-100" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>I follow someone new</b> — their old posts are not in my feed. <i>Fix:</i> backfill their latest ~20 posts into my feed once (a small pull-then-push)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="95" width="445" x="40" y="2060" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-101" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Unfollow or delete a post</b> — scrubbing millions of feeds is too costly. <i>Fix:</i> leave the IDs, filter them out when hydrating (post missing or unfollowed = skipped)." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="95" width="445" x="512" y="2060" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-102" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Redis feed is lost</b> — it is a cache, not the truth. <i>Fix:</i> rebuild from Follows + Posts, newest first. Slower for a moment, never wrong." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="95" width="445" x="984" y="2060" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-103" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=10;fillColor=#f5f5f5;strokeColor=#666666;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Inactive user returns</b> — we stopped maintaining their feed. <i>Fix:</i> build it on login with a pull, then resume push." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="95" width="445" x="1456" y="2060" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-104" parent="1" style="text;html=1;whiteSpace=wrap;align=left;verticalAlign=top;fontSize=16;fontColor=#222222;fontStyle=1;spacing=4;" value="How to read it" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="30" width="900" x="40" y="2380" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-105" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Write path (①–⑤)</b><br>① Save the post and its media. ② Publish an event; the user is done.<br>③ A worker finds the author's followers. ④ Fewer than ~10k? ⑤a Push the post_id into each follower's Redis feed. More than that? ⑤b Skip — the post waits in the author's timeline.<br><br><b>Read path (⑥–⑪)</b><br>⑥ Read my feed from Redis. ⑦ Find the celebrities I follow. ⑧ Pull their latest posts. ⑨ Merge by time. ⑩ Rank and hydrate. ⑪ Return one page with a cursor.<br><br><b>Example:</b> a friend (300 followers) posts → 300 quick Redis inserts. A cricketer (50M followers) posts → nothing is pushed; each follower's next app open pulls it in ~one extra lookup." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="420" width="610" x="40" y="2420" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-106" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Architect decisions — say "why A over B"</b><br>1. Hybrid fan-out over pure push or pure pull.<br>2. Work at write time, where the multiplier is small (reads are ~50× more frequent).<br>3. Feed stores IDs only: tiny, and edits/deletes show instantly.<br>4. Each data type goes in the store that matches how it is READ.<br>5. Follows indexed in both directions: fan-out needs followers, the feed needs followees.<br>6. Time-sortable post IDs: chronological order for free, no created_at index.<br>7. Celebrity threshold is a dial between write cost and read cost.<br>8. Everything after saving the post is async (Kafka): the user never waits for fan-out.<br>9. Chronological first; ranking as a second stage once there is data.<br>10. Counts (likes) are eventually consistent; the feed is a rebuildable cache." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="420" width="610" x="670" y="2420" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="kCWay35iT9l1axRZK1Bq-107" parent="1" style="rounded=1;arcSize=6;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fontSize=12;fillColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#999999;strokeWidth=1.5;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacingLeft=8;spacingRight=8;spacingTop=2;spacingBottom=2;" value="<b>Mental model &amp; interview close</b><br><i>Post → Event → Fan-out (push or pull) → Feed IDs → Merge → Rank → Hydrate → Page</i><br><br><b>Trade-offs we accept</b><br>• Hybrid → two code paths and a merge step<br>• Push → write amplification and RAM cost for Redis<br>• Feed, search and counts → eventually consistent<br>• Every index → slower writes and more storage<br>• Ranking → ML cost, harder debugging, filter-bubble risk<br>• Celebrity posts → one extra pull at read time<br><br><b>One-line close:</b> "Fan-out is a choice of WHERE to pay: once at write time, or many times at read time. Use the cheaper side for each author, and keep the feed as a rebuildable cache of IDs."<br><br><b>Honest test:</b> a 50M-follower celebrity posts during a cricket final — does fan-out grind for 18 minutes? It must not: nothing is pushed, followers pull it when they open the app." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="420" width="630" x="1300" y="2420" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: Social Media Feed — Data Model, Indexing & Fan-out

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1862px; height: 1px; padding-top: 62px; margin-left: 30px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Goal: show every user a fast home feed of posts from people they follow | Rule: reads outnumber writes ~50:1, so do the heavy work when someone POSTS | Example scale (assumed): 100M daily users × 10 opens ≈ 11.5k feed reads/s (peak ~35k) · 20M posts/day ≈ 230/s · 200 avg followers → 4B feed inserts/day ≈ 46k/s

rect.style: stroke: light-dark(rgb(178, 106, 0), rgb(195, 133, 42));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1896px; height: 1px; padding-top: 103px; margin-left: 15px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #b26a00;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#b26a00, #c3852a); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: START HERE — the one question this design answers

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(248, 206, 204), rgb(81, 45, 43)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(184, 84, 80), rgb(215, 129, 126));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 175px; margin-left: 31px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Problem: a home feed = newest posts from the ~500 people I follow. Building it on EVERY open means a lookup across 500 authors plus a sort — too slow for 1B opens a day.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 175px; margin-left: 671px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Decision: do the work when someone POSTS (write path), so opening the app (read path) is one fast lookup.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 572px; height: 1px; padding-top: 175px; margin-left: 1311px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: But: a celebrity post would need 50M feed inserts. So the plan is a HYBRID: push for normal users, pull for celebrities.

path.style: stroke: light-dark(rgb(26, 86, 160), rgb(124, 176, 239));
fill: light-dark(rgb(26, 86, 160), rgb(124, 176, 239)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(26, 86, 160), rgb(124, 176, 239));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding-top: 175px; margin-left: 636px;

div.div: so

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1896px; height: 1px; padding-top: 263px; margin-left: 15px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #1a56a0;
display: inline-block; font-size: 14px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#1a56a0, #7cb0ef); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; font-weight: bold; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: A · DATA — which store for which data, and how each is indexed

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1794px; height: 1px; padding-top: 291px; margin-left: 25px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #222222;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#222222, #d0d0d0); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Blue = the table and its columns · Green = how it is indexed · Yellow = why this store, and what it costs

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 392px; margin-left: 31px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
1 · USERS — SQL
users(
user_id PK, handle UNIQUE, email UNIQUE,
display_name, created_at,
follower_count, is_celebrity)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 542px; margin-left: 31px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: B-tree on user_id + UNIQUE B-tree on handle and email. Answers "find user at login" in one lookup, and no two people can own one handle.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 677px; margin-left: 31px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Why SQL: small data that needs strong consistency. Cost: hard to shard — fine, users are our smallest table.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 392px; margin-left: 346px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
2 · FOLLOWS — SQL or wide-column
follows(follower_id, followee_id, created_at)
copy A: PK (follower_id, followee_id)
copy B: PK (followee_id, follower_id)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 542px; margin-left: 346px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Two composite indexes, one per direction. A answers "who do I follow?", B answers "who follows me?" (fan-out needs it). One index cannot serve both.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 677px; margin-left: 346px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Why not a graph DB? We only need 1-hop lists. Cost: every follow = 2 writes. Add a graph DB later only for "people you may know".

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 392px; margin-left: 661px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
3 · POSTS — wide-column / sharded SQL
posts(post_id PK, author_id, text,
media_ids, created_at, like_count…)
post_id = time-sortable ID (Snowflake-style)

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 542px; margin-left: 661px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: PK post_id → get one post. (author_id, post_id DESC) → a profile page, already sorted. Time-sortable IDs mean NO extra created_at index.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 677px; margin-left: 661px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Why NoSQL: huge, append-heavy, read by key. Cost: no ad-hoc joins — every new question needs its own table or index.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(218, 232, 252), rgb(29, 41, 59)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(108, 142, 191), rgb(92, 121, 163));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 392px; margin-left: 976px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
4 · FEED — Redis sorted set
key = feed:{user_id}
member = post_id
score = post time (or rank score)
keep only the newest ~800 ids

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(213, 232, 212), rgb(31, 47, 30)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(130, 179, 102), rgb(68, 110, 44));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 542px; margin-left: 976px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Sorted set (skip list): ZREVRANGE returns a page in O(log N + page). IDs only — tiny; bodies come from a post cache.

div.b: THE SIX QUESTIONS — answered with their trade-offs

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1915px; margin-left: 31px;

div.div: Push or pull? HYBRID. Push (fan-out on write) for normal authors, pull (fan-out on read) for celebrities. Why: push makes reads instant; pull avoids 50M writes per post. Cost: two code paths and a merge step.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1915px; margin-left: 346px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Fan-out on write vs on read? On write, cost = followers per POST (4B inserts/day — fine). On read, cost = followees per OPEN (1B opens × 500 lookups — too much). So: pay at write while the multiplier is small.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1915px; margin-left: 661px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Celebrity with 50M followers? One post = 50M inserts — at 46k/s that is ~18 minutes of the whole fleet, mostly into inactive feeds. Skip push above the threshold; readers pull. Extra saving: push only to followers active in the last ~7 days.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1915px; margin-left: 976px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: How is the home feed generated? Precomputed ID list in Redis (⑤a) + pulled celebrity posts (⑧), merged (⑨), hydrated (⑩). Why IDs only: the list is tiny, and edits or deletes show instantly because bodies are read fresh.

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1915px; margin-left: 1291px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: Chronological or recommended? Start chronological: simple, explainable, cheap (sort by post_id). Recommended: better engagement, but costly ML, hard to debug, filter-bubble risk. Offer both: "Following" and "For you".

rect.style: fill: light-dark(rgb(255, 242, 204), rgb(40, 29, 0)); stroke: light-dark(rgb(214, 182, 86), rgb(109, 81, 0));

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 257px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1915px; margin-left: 1606px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 10px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: How do we rank? Two stages: (1) a cheap candidate pool (~500 from feed + celebrities), (2) score = recency × closeness to author × engagement × post type, then diversify so one author cannot dominate. Budget: ~50–100 ms.

div.div: How to read it

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 2622px; margin-left: 31px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Write path (①–⑤)
① Save the post and its media. ② Publish an event; the user is done.
③ A worker finds the author's followers. ④ Fewer than ~10k? ⑤a Push the post_id into each follower's Redis feed. More than that? ⑤b Skip — the post waits in the author's timeline.
Read path (⑥–⑪)
⑥ Read my feed from Redis. ⑦ Find the celebrities I follow. ⑧ Pull their latest posts. ⑨ Merge by time. ⑩ Rank and hydrate. ⑪ Return one page with a cursor.
Example: a friend (300 followers) posts → 300 quick Redis inserts. A cricketer (50M followers) posts → nothing is pushed; each follower's next app open pulls it in ~one extra lookup.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 592px; height: 1px; padding-top: 2622px; margin-left: 661px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#000000, #ffffff); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Architect decisions — say "why A over B"
1. Hybrid fan-out over pure push or pure pull.
2. Work at write time, where the multiplier is small (reads are ~50× more frequent).
3. Feed stores IDs only: tiny, and edits/deletes show instantly.
4. Each data type goes in the store that matches how it is READ.
5. Follows indexed in both directions: fan-out needs followers, the feed needs followees.
6. Time-sortable post IDs: chronological order for free, no created_at index.
7. Celebrity threshold is a dial between write cost and read cost.
8. Everything after saving the post is async (Kafka): the user never waits for fan-out.
9. Chronological first; ranking as a second stage once there is data.
10. Counts (likes) are eventually consistent; the feed is a rebuildable cache.

div.div:
Mental model & interview close
Post → Event → Fan-out (push or pull) → Feed IDs → Merge → Rank → Hydrate → Page
Trade-offs we accept
• Hybrid → two code paths and a merge step
• Push → write amplification and RAM cost for Redis
• Feed, search and counts → eventually consistent
• Every index → slower writes and more storage
• Ranking → ML cost, harder debugging, filter-bubble risk
• Celebrity posts → one extra pull at read time
One-line close: "Fan-out is a choice of WHERE to pay: once at write time, or many times at read time. Use the cheaper side for each author, and keep the feed as a rebuildable cache of IDs."
Honest test: a 50M-follower celebrity posts during a cricket final — does fan-out grind for 18 minutes? It must not: nothing is pushed, followers pull it when they open the app.
